Kuali Basics
Kuali Basics
Quick Links

Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is URI’s system for managing university curriculum and the curriculum approval process. It uses electronic forms and workflow to route course, program, and specialization proposals through the appropriate levels of review and approval.

Kuali serves as the central source for approved curriculum information:
Kuali CM — Manages curriculum proposals and the approval workflow.
Academic Catalog — Pulls approved course, program, and specialization information from Kuali.
eCampus — Receives approved course information from Kuali for implementation in future terms.

Information entered into Kuali can flow directly into the official academic catalog and eCampus. Proposals should therefore be clear, accurate, and unambiguous, as the information entered during the proposal process becomes part of the University’s official curriculum.
Access to Kuali CM is limited to faculty, Deans, and select administrators and staff. Only faculty members may submit curriculum proposals.

Faculty members automatically have access to Kuali CM, as faculty are the users authorized to submit curricular proposals. If this is your first time accessing Kuali CM, sign in using your URI Microsoft 365 account.

Access to Kuali CM is also available to deans and select administrators or staff. In specific cases, other non-faculty users may request access.
Use the Kuali Access Package to request access using your URI SSO. After selecting Continue, you will be asked to provide your job or position title and a business justification for needing access. Once your request has been reviewed, you will be notified whether access has been granted.

Sign in to your Microsoft 365 Apps using your URI SSO.
Select Kuali Course Management from your application collection.
Alternatively, use the direct link to Kuali CM and bookmark it for future access.
Once logged in, select the Curriculum tile. This is where you can view current courses, programs, and specializations and, for authorized users, create proposals for new or modified curriculum.
When you enter Curriculum Management, the Dashboard serves as your homepage. It provides quick access to your proposals and items requiring your action.

My Proposals allows you to:
Continue working on Drafts you have started but not yet submitted.
View submitted proposals and their current workflow status.
Access proposals directly from the Dashboard.
Any proposals you begin but have not yet submitted will appear as Drafts. From this section, you can continue editing or delete a draft.
Select View All to see your complete list of proposals. The list can be filtered, downloaded, and printed.

My Action List displays your ten most recent items requiring action. These may include proposals that require you to:
Review and approve
Acknowledge
Edit and return to the workflow after being sent back by a reviewing committee
Use the navigation bar on the left side of the screen to access courses, programs, specializations, and proposals, including drafts, proposals under review, and approved records.

Use the search bar at the top of the Courses, Programs, Specializations, or Proposals pages to locate specific records. Use the filters on the right side of the page to narrow your results.
Status: Select Active when searching for current curricular items. Retired and Inactive statuses are not consistently used in Kuali CM.
Groups: Use Groups to locate curricular records associated with a specific department or college.

Kuali uses colored bars to indicate which version of a curricular record you are viewing.
🟢 Current Version — The version currently in effect. For most records, the earliest version available in Kuali is Fall 2022, when URI began using Kuali. Earlier historical versions are available in eCampus.
⚪ Past Version — An earlier version of the record, including inactive records.
🟣 Future Version — A version scheduled to become active in a future term.
↕️ Use the arrows next to the term dates to expand the record history and select an earlier or future version.

The status indicators below apply only when you are viewing a proposal and not the curricular record itself. The colored bar at the top of a proposal indicates where the proposal is in the curriculum approval workflow.
🟡 Draft — A new proposal or proposed change that has been created but not yet submitted to the workflow. Drafts can be edited or deleted.
🔵 Under Review — A proposal that has been submitted to the workflow and is currently moving through the approval process.
⚫ Denied — A proposal that has been denied during the review process. Denied proposals cannot be edited or resubmitted.
🟢 Approved — A proposal that has completed the required approval process and has been approved.
Tip: When viewing an approved proposal, you can switch to the current curricular record by selecting “View Active Course (Program / Specialization).”

Method of Instruction
Tags: courses
Short Description: The instructional delivery method. Also known as "class component.”
Method of Instruction
Provided below is the complete list of approved methods of instruction, as proposed in FSEC Report #2024-2025-03 and subsequently approved by the Faculty Senate through Bill #24-25-12 on January 23, 2025.
A course in which the primary method is presentation and students are expected to participate in a variety of ways, such as small-group discussions, questions and answers, writing-exercises, etc.
Applied course work, generally involving experimentation or observation, typically using special equipment (including computers and specialized software).
Separate sections of a lecture course regularly scheduled for discussion.
Supervised work with an emphasis on performance and creativity in which faculty instruct, assist, and critique.
Course offered to a small group (usually no more than 20 students) where participants actively exchange ideas and findings based on readings or research.

One-on-one instruction in which the student enters into an agreement with the instructor that defines the focus of inquiry and nature of activities. Includes tutorials, directed readings, special projects.
Structured experiences where the primary aim is to connect theory with practice. Includes clinics, internships, externships, student teaching, field experiences. May include regular class meetings.
Similar to a seminar, with emphasis on applied rather than theoretical learning, but not offered for degree-program credit.

Bachelor Degree Requirements
Tags: programs
Short Description: The university-wide academic and residency requirements students must meet to earn a bachelor’s degree from URI.
Bachelor Degree Requirements

Complete of a minimum of 120 credits (some majors require more)
Earn a minimum overall grade point average of 2.00 (some majors require a higher overall GPA)
Complete the coursework and other requirements for the curriculum of the major with the minimum grades per course and overall grade point averages for that major, or portions of that major, as specified in the section of the catalog which describes the requirements for each major
Complete General Education requirements, as specified elsewhere in this catalog
Abide by community standards as defined in the University Manual and Student Handbook
Complete the senior year in residence at URI
Earn one half of the total number of credits needed in the major at URI (same for a minor, if one is being pursued)
Transfer no more than half of the credits required for graduation from a two-year institution
Earn at least one-fourth of the credits required for graduation in-residence at URI (usually at least 30 credits)*
Students should review all major/degree requirements with their academic advisor to ensure completion of all course, credit and GPA minimums.

Degrees & Majors
Tags: programs
Short Description: Degrees are academic credentials awarded by the University, while majors are a student’s concentrated field of study within a degree program.
Degrees & Majors

Undergraduate programs are required to have a minimum or 120 credits, and a maximum of 148 (UM 8.21.10)
Undergraduate programs shall include at least 6 credits of free electives (UM 8.21.10)
General Education requirements shall apply to all undergraduate programs (UM 8.21.11)
A cumulative average of at least 2.00 is required to graduate from all undergraduate degrees. (UM 8.22.10)
Master’s degree programs with thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. 18 must be from content-based courses, 6 must be thesis courses. (GSM 7.44.1)
Master’s degree programs without thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. (GSM 7.45.1)
Doctoral students must complete a Program of Study with a minimum of 64 credit hours beyond the undergraduate degree (GSM 7.54) (See GSM sections 7.54 and 7.21)
In Kuali, the term program refers to all credential types; Degrees, majors, minors, and certificates. In the Manual, program refers to a graduate student’s major field of study.
